answer:
Undistributed reportable income (ERI) is generally taxable as **income** for the UK tax year in which the fund’s reporting period ends, even if not paid out. Keep the fund’s ERI statements; amounts already taxed can generally be added to the acquisition cost (or otherwise relieved) when calculating a later disposal gain, to avoid taxing the same value twice.

On disposal, the gain is generally within **capital gains tax** rules, not offshore-income-gain treatment, because the ETF had UK reporting-fund status throughout your ownership. Calculate the gain under UK rules, including allowable costs and any ERI basis adjustment; annual exemptions, rates and loss rules may apply. Check the fund’s reporting data and your tax-year circumstances, and obtain advice for your specific return.
